category_title: Young children with persistent challenging behaviors and communication delays
minimal_context: Kayden and his mother are at home in the evening, and she prompts him to start getting ready for bed.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Kayden, it is time to start to get ready for bed.

STUDENT: (Starts crying) No!

TUTOR: Come on, we need to get ready for bed now.

STUDENT: (Cries louder)

TUTOR: Stop crying and let's go.

STUDENT: (Screams and starts hitting)

options.A: Consistently use full language to describe all materials and activities to Kayden throughout the duration of the evening bedtime routine.
options.B: Support Kayden's needs through shared power by compromising, negotiating situations, or sharing decisions with him instead of trying to impose control over his behaviors during the bedtime routine.
options.C: Incorporate opportunities to give attention to Kayden during appropriate activities just before bedtime, focusing on positive interactions in mutually enjoyable activities like playing low-energy games.
options.D: Provide simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication in the perspective of total communication for Kayden throughout the duration of the evening bedtime routine.
